cim: The AI boom is forecast to increase data center emissions by 70% by 2030
cim_eredeti: The AI boom is forecast to increase data center emissions by 70% by 2030
szoveg_eredeti:
A new report from the International Energy Agency (IEA) warns that electricity consumption by the world’s data centers is expected to nearly double in the next four years, according to The Guardian.

The world’s existing data centers currently have a capacity of about 120 gigawatts. According to the IEA, an additional 120 gigawatts could be added by 2030. The expansion of artificial intelligence is expected to account for about 75% of that increase.

At the same time, carbon dioxide emissions from data centers risk increasing by 70%. This is despite the fact that data center companies are among the world’s largest corporate buyers of renewable energy.

In the US, natural gas is projected to account for about 60% of data centers’ electricity supply by 2030. In China, however, coal-fired power is expected to account for about half of data centers’ electricity supply. IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol also warns that the energy market is in a historically uncertain situation following the war in the Middle East.
